items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: With our group there were ... Jimmie Daniels, a singer.

ctx.x: Like most Americans I had never drunk wine with my meals. The passengers could have as many bottles as they desired and I drank one white and two red ones with my first meal. After that I started drinking two white and two red bottles with every meal. I only ate twice a day although there was breakfast, dinner, afternoon tea and supper. I was never awake in time to have breakfast and tea did not interest me. I was drinking eight quarts of wine a day and was never drunk. But I was quite gay for the whole trip…

With our group there were two chorus girls, Ethel Moses and Mary Hart, Freddy 'Snake Hips' Taylor, Lucky's wife Clara Townsend, Booker's wife Joyce, and Jimmie Daniels, a singer. The band rehearsed every day, we swam in the pool on deck and played cards at night. The trip was fine and the weather beautiful.

We arrived at Gibraltar and small boats came out to the ship with souvenirs to sell and kids dived in the water to retrieve pieces of money that the passengers threw to them. Gibraltar was very interesting to see

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Freddy Taylor, Mary Hart, Ethel Moses and Jimmy Daniels were also included in the show which Lucky and Madriguara's orchestras accompanied.

ctx.x: Then we sailed into the Mediterranean Sea and the next day I saw schools of dolphin and flying fish which I watched for hours. The dolphins would follow a boat for miles. We stopped at Naples, Italy, the 9th July, and it was possible to visit some of the city. On July 10th we disembarked at Ville- and went by special bus to Monte Carlo. The houses looked different and so many other things made me know that I really was in a foreign country, 4053 miles from New York.

Rehearsals for the show to be put on at the Sporting d'Ete began the day after our arrival and included the orchestra of Henri Madriguara who featured Latin American music, and Bela de Racz, a Hungarian orchestra. There were also 16 dancing and show girls, most of whom had been in the Ziegfeld Follies, plus the stars who were Gloria Grafton, a singer, Carl Randall, a dancer, Tito Coral, a singer, the Arnaut Brothers who did a violin act imitating birds, Reva Rayes, a Mexican girl singer, Moha_med Ben Jamai, an…

This was an amazing orchestra because they played Hungarian gypsy music which I had never heard before, using a which looked like a small piano but was played with mallets. There were 3 violinists, 2 viols and bass violin. I really enjoyed listening to this orchestra whose musicians got a big kick out of listening to us when we played jazzy dance numbers.
